_acquisition.pokemon_home: Pokemon HOME has ALWAYS been a way into Champions - it is not a new mechanic and nothing about the game changed. A Pokemon arriving this way is PERMANENT (trainable at once, no VP, no ticket) and never touches the rental list. Sableye came in this way on 2026-08-31. It is the only route that delivers a CHOSEN species on purpose, so it is the only plannable one. HOME also works in the other direction: Sableye was sent back out to HOME on 2026-08-31 to free a box slot, so a Pokemon parked there is not lost - it is storage, and it can come back permanent.

_origin_rule.rule: A Pokemon's ORIGIN decides whether it can ever leave the Champions box, and this is the single most important fact about box management. CHAMPIONS-ORIGIN (anything from an Encounter, whether taken as a rental or bought outright for 2500 VP or with a permanence ticket) CAN NEVER BE SENT TO HOME. It occupies its slot until it is RELEASED, which destroys it. HOME-ORIGIN (caught in Pokemon GO, sent to HOME, then into Champions) CAN GO BACK OUT TO HOME at any time and come back later. Only HOME-origin Pokemon make the box elastic.
_origin_rule.the_pipeline: GO --one way--> HOME <==> Champions   ||   Encounter --> Champions, and stuck there.
_origin_rule.why_it_matters: 'Permanent' in Champions has been recorded in this file as if it were the good state. It is not. Buying a rental for 2500 VP or spending a permanence ticket does NOT create a real permanent - it creates a Champions-origin Pokemon that clogs a slot forever. The player's word for it: it 'me sigue impidiendo manejar correctamente caja'. A HOME-origin Pokemon is the only true permanent, because losing a box slot never loses the Pokemon.
_origin_rule.the_players_plan: Gradually REPLACE Champions-origin Pokemon with their own Pokemon GO catches routed through HOME. This is a standing, long-running goal, not a one-off. So when a box Pokemon has a HOME counterpart, the HOME one is NOT a spare or a duplicate - IT IS THE REAL ONE, and the box copy is the clog to clear. Never again describe a HOME copy as a 'spare'.
consequences_for_advice: Never present 'make this rental permanent for 2500 VP' as an upgrade without saying it locks the slot forever.
The 5 permanence tickets have the same problem: a ticket spent on a rental buys a permanent clog. Spending one is a real trade-off now, not free value.
Training VP sunk into a Champions-origin Pokemon is spent on something that can never be parked. That does not make it wasted - it plays fine - but it is not an argument for keeping the slot.
When weighing a release, the sunk training VP is only one side. The other side is a slot that becomes elastic forever.
_origin_rule.unknown: The ORIGIN OF EACH POKEMON ALREADY IN THE BOX IS NOT RECORDED. Sableye was HOME-origin and was sent back out on 2026-08-31, which is why that round trip worked. Everything currently listed is assumed Champions-origin unless the player says otherwise - ASK rather than guessing, and record the answer here as it is learned.
_origin_rule.training_survives_the_round_trip: Player, 2026-09-08. A HOME-ORIGIN Pokemon trained inside Champions KEEPS THAT TRAINING FOREVER. Sent back out it looks like an ordinary HOME Pokemon again, but HOME stores the Champions metadata, so when it returns to Champions the moves, nature, ability and SP are all still there. THE ROUND TRIP COSTS NOTHING AND LOSES NO VP. This is what actually makes the box elastic: a HOME-origin build can be parked to free a slot and recalled later fully intact, as many times as needed.
_origin_rule.what_the_swap_really_costs: Training does NOT transfer between two different Pokemon, so replacing a built Champions-origin Pokemon with its HOME counterpart still means training the HOME one from scratch - about 1830 VP for a four-move, 66-SP, nature-changed build. But that is a ONE-TIME cost, paid once and never again, because from then on that build can be parked and recalled for free. The Champions-origin copy's 1830 VP, by contrast, is welded to a slot that can only be freed by destroying the Pokemon. So the swap is not 'lose 1830 VP', it is 'pay 1830 VP once to turn a permanently locked slot into a reusable one'.
